hero.title: Public Health in Switzerland for Indian Students
hero.subtitle: **Public Health in Switzerland for Indian Students** offers an opportunity to develop the knowledge and skills needed to improve population health, prevent diseases, analyse health data, evaluate healthcare systems, and design public health programmes. Swiss universities offer opportunities to explore epidemiology, global health, health policy, biostatistics, health promotion, and public health research.

overview:
Students who want to **Study Public Health in Switzerland** can explore programmes at different academic levels and gain exposure to international health research and healthcare systems. Switzerland is home to international health organisations and research institutions, making it a relevant destination for students interested in global health and international development. However, Public Health is different from clinical medical training: an MPH or related degree does not qualify a graduate to practise as a doctor.

For programme research and application planning, students can also connect with **Edu-Hawk Worldwide**.

faq.question: Can Indian students study Public Health in Switzerland?
faq.answer: Yes, Indian students can explore suitable programmes, provided they meet the institution’s academic, language, and application requirements. Eligibility should be confirmed directly with the university.

faq.question: Is IELTS required for Public Health in Switzerland?
faq.answer: It depends on the programme and the applicant’s educational background. English-taught programmes may require proof of English proficiency or accept specified exemptions. Check the university’s official requirements before booking a test.

faq.question: How long does a Public Health degree take in Switzerland?
faq.answer: The duration depends on the qualification. The University of Geneva’s MSc in Global Health takes two years full-time, while the joint Master of Public Health coordinated by Swiss TPH is part-time and can be completed over two to five years.

faq.question: What is the cost of studying Public Health in Switzerland?
faq.answer: Costs vary by institution and programme. For example, the University of Geneva lists tuition of CHF 500 per semester for its MSc in Global Health, while the joint MPH coordinated by Swiss TPH has a published total course fee of approximately CHF 39,000. Living expenses are additional.

faq.question: What jobs can I get after studying Public Health in Switzerland?
faq.answer: Possible career paths include public health research, epidemiology, health policy, programme management, health data analysis, and work with NGOs or international health organisations. Employment depends on your qualifications, experience, language skills, and work authorisation.
